newsitem.title: JAPAN: Drought-hit N.Korea reports 100 mm rainfall.
newsitem.headline: Drought-hit N.Korea reports 100 mm rainfall.

text.p: Drought-stricken areas of North Korea received more than 100 mm (4 inches) of rain overnight, state media reported on Sunday.
According to a weather update on Korean Central Broadcasting, more than 100 mm of rain fell on North and South Pyongan provinces and on North Hwanghae province.
Other areas, including the region surrounding the capital Pyongyang, also received rain, said the report, monitored by Radiopress, a Tokyo-based news agency.

The communist state's official press recently said a heat wave currently afflicting the country was the worst in 61 years and said the subsequent drought was causing serious damage to agriculture and other sectors of the national economy.
Devastating floods in 1994 and 1995 washed away a substantial portion of North Korea's crop acreage, pushing the country to the brink of famine, hunger experts have said.
International aid agencies have stepped up food appeals for the Stalinist state, warning of imminent starvation, particularly among small children.
The Rome-based U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) launched a fresh appeal earlier this month for $46 million in food aid for North Korea on top of an earlier request for $95.5 million.
